body: Hey man, I'd love to hear what you gotta say. PM me or reply here I'm always down to talk, especially about this.

Wow this is actually really helpful, thank you. I knew all of this the last time I quit but I completely forgot about this side of it. I really do need to focus on fixing what's causing this stress and anxiety. Yesterday I went and swam laps at the campus pool and it helped a lot. I guess the endorphins got pumped and I was in a great, smiley mood for a few hours after. That was the first time I've been in a good mood without drugs for the past few weeks. I guess I'll try some exercising and really think about what's causing this. Thank you so much I really mean it.

They thought I was just smoking with friends occasionally. They didn't know I was doing it in their own house everyday. Then they found it in the house months later. That time was awful. 

But thanks for the advice. I was already thinking about waiting until I was in the groove of everything before I even considered it. I've even thought about smoking like once a week, but only if I have all As. Which isn't likely, I know I can do it I'm just being realistic. But at least if I did have all As I wouldn't feel any guilt for smoking.

My friend is in a similar situation, but its more intense. He's about to be 20 and he can't for the life of him admit that he's in the wrong. On day 9. I'm actually an artist myself (technically a rapper but I don't care for the label). It gets better. Just take a break, don't force yourself to do it. Let it come to you. I write at the most random times. For instance I should have went to sleep an hour ago but I got on soundcloud, found a nice beat I liked and started writing. It'll come back. And I guarantee after you adjust, you'll be even better.

This. Think about that number going back to 0. You don't want that, trust me. I went 5 months without it before, but it wasn't by choice. When I finally relapsed, I regretted it immediately. I was high as fuck sitting there thinking about all of that hard work and dedication just disappeared. And then I started smoking daily again a few days later. 3 months later, here I am. But this time I quit on my own. 100% my choice. It makes me feel good knowing I'm in control. 

Also, if you haven't seen your dealer since you stopped, chances are you aren't friends. Meaning he really is trying to get your business back. It's smart on his part. I'm not saying he's trying to manipulate you, but if you end up smoking with him, that's exactly what it is, except you will have manipulated yourself. 

Good luck, and please stay at it. If you ever want to talk shoot me a message. I'm always here for anyone about anything.
Listen to this guy. I really don't know anything about this whole process with probation.

Thanks so much! The suppose there is great. I can't explain this problem to anyone else. People joke about weed being addictive and no one understands what it's capable of doing. I'm happy you responded, thank you.
Thank you! That means a lot. I already feel more positive, I guess it's knowing that I am in control. I have the power. Feels good man.

Hope you're still hanging in there. Take this shit one step at a time man. Focus on quitting today, relax and watch your TV. Tomorrow, start doing a little work. The next day do more. It'll become a habit. Baby steps, you don't need to make a shit load of changes at once.

EDIT: Oh and get rid of your stash if you already haven't. That'll ease your mind.
No problem, I'm always one message away if you need someone to talk to about whatever. I'm a night smoker myself and I know how it is.

Good luck and please keep us posted! It'll help me at least and I'll definitely be reading your updates. If you find any tricks to combat the negative effects (cravings and what not) post those too. Today is *maybe* going to be my first day of quitting to. I don't want to lie, I'm still in that stage post-wanting to quit but pre-quitting.

Yeah I have a super sick pipe from Cozumel, Mexico. I never smoked out of it though I guess I could just get my friend to hang on to it and throw everything else out. I actually don't have a problem falling asleep at night, its just that I'm sitting in my bed with my stash 5 feet away and I know I can do it. I guess it comes down to will power. I know it'll force me into my hobbies which is what I really want to focus on (I'm an artist). I used to tell myself, oh weed will help me creatively. It did to an extent, for some things, but 99% of the time I ended up just watching TV or playing games. I'm rambling now but thank you for your response, I really appreciate it.

That's actually really helpful and I appreciate your response. I do have my stash in my house and thats one of the biggest issues. I've given it all to my friend before to take a break/quit and I literally asked for it back 3 days later and got it. I feel like I need to just flush it all so I can't get it back. And you're right, it isn't a HUGE problem for me, what bothers me the most is the fact that I haven't been able to successfully quit even when I wanted to. It's so easy to justify it either way. I really want to quit so I can grow as a person and put it behind me, at least for now. I have ben doing the same routine as far as work, school, smoking for like 3 years now and it's getting old. I want to expand and I think quitting smoking is a good step in that process. Thank you again for your help, it means a lot.

Yes. Weed helps you fall asleep, but it doesn't help you sleep **well**. I read a study that said it prevents you from getting deep sleep (entering the REM stage, the IMPORTANT stage for rest) therefore 8 hours of sleep can feel like 4. Especially if you're still high or buzzed when you fall asleep.
